novel_features.name: Lab Citation Impact Rank
novel_features.description: Rank researchers at your institution by citation impact within a specific Lancet journal or topic.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a full author-citation graph pre-materialized locally from OpenAlex; external APIs cannot cross-tab instantly across journals.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Grant managers and department heads use this to identify who is leading at your institution in a specific field; agents can use it to find high-impact collaborators.

novel_features.name: Institutional Citation Mesh
novel_features.description: Find researchers at your institution who co-author Lancet papers and quantify how their work connects.
novel_features.rationale: Requires author identity resolution and a co-authorship graph built from OpenAlex authorships; impossible without a pre-synced local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Librarians and research directors use this to uncover collaboration opportunities and map how an institution's researchers connect through Lancet.

novel_features.name: Affiliation Growth Tracking
novel_features.description: Track institutions gaining publication velocity in Lancet journals; identify rising research centers.
novel_features.rationale: Requires per-year institutional publication counts derived from OpenAlex authorship+date data; point-in-time API queries cannot reveal multi-year trends.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Strategy teams track this to understand competitive research landscapes and identify emerging partner institutions.

novel_features.name: Editorial Drift Detector
novel_features.description: Compare how a journal's topic distribution shifts between two time windows; spot emerging and fading specialties.
novel_features.rationale: Requires stored topic-tagged works across windows; no API serves comparative topic-distribution queries for arbitrary windows.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Research strategists use this to align their work with journal editorial priorities and detect when journal scope shifts.

novel_features.name: Reading List Curation
novel_features.description: Auto-generate ranked reading lists for a topic, sorted by date/citations/relevance, exportable as Markdown or BibTeX.
novel_features.rationale: Fast local ranking on tens of thousands of articles with multi-dimensional sort requires a pre-indexed local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Librarians and researchers use this to quickly assemble authoritative reading lists without manual screening.

novel_features.name: Citation Visibility Gap
novel_features.description: Find authors whose citation impact is out of step with the prestige of the Lancet journals they publish in.
novel_features.rationale: Requires cross-tabulating per-author citation counts against per-journal prestige from the local OpenAlex store; three aggregates impossible in one API call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Grant managers and research directors use this to identify under-recognized talent for promotion or collaboration.

narrative.headline: Search Lancet articles offline and analyze author impact, institutional networks, and editorial trends — powered by the free OpenAlex scholarly graph.
narrative.value_prop: The Lancet CLI gives researchers and institutions offline access to The Lancet family of journals via OpenAlex. Beyond search and fetch, it ranks researchers by citation impact within a specialty (rank-authors), maps institutional co-authorship networks (mesh), tracks which institutions are publishing more over time (affiliation-growth), and detects how a journal's editorial focus shifts (drift) — insights impossible from single API queries or paywalled tools.

quickstart.comment: Verify the CLI is working and OpenAlex is reachable (no auth required)
Find recent Lancet articles on a research topic (scoped to Lancet journals by default)
Build the local database from OpenAlex so the analytics commands below can run offline
Rank the most-cited authors in a specific Lancet journal
See how the journal's editorial focus has shifted between two periods

troubleshoots.fix: Run refresh first: thelancet-pp-cli refresh --journal lancet (analytics read the local OpenAlex-derived store)

troubleshoots.symptom: rank-authors or mesh returns empty for an institution
troubleshoots.fix: Institution names match OpenAlex display names; try a distinctive substring like 'Oxford' rather than a full legal name or acronym
OpenAlex allows ~10 req/s; lower --rate-limit or set a contact email via OPENALEX_MAILTO to join the polite pool

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI to answer questions about The Lancet's research landscape offline and without API throttling: literature reviews, tracking institutional publication trends, finding collaborators, and analyzing how medical research evolves over time.
anti_triggers: Do NOT use this CLI for real-time article feeds or breaking news; it syncs periodically from OpenAlex, not continuously
Do NOT use this for journal submission or peer-review status; it mirrors published works, not the editorial pipeline
Do NOT use this for full-text access to paywalled articles; it returns metadata, topics, and links only

recipes.title: Build a topic reading list for a literature review
recipes.command: thelancet-pp-cli curate --topic 'machine learning diagnosis' --sort citations --output bibtex > review.bib
recipes.explanation: Generate a citation-ranked, BibTeX-exportable reading list on a topic across Lancet journals in one command.

recipes.title: Narrow a deeply nested works response for an agent
recipes.explanation: OpenAlex works are large and deeply nested; pair --agent with dotted --select paths to return only the fields you need and save context.

recipes.title: Spot editorial drift in a specialty journal
recipes.explanation: Compare topic distributions across two multi-year windows to see which specialties the journal now publishes more or less of.

trigger_phrases: rank the top authors in Lancet
how has this journal's focus changed
